_purpose: Authored contract stating what each graded CI step MUST ACTUALLY EXECUTE (Gate 4N-I24C, findings I24C-06 and I24C-07).
_why_this_file_exists: I23 asserted CI wiring with `assert "scripts/x.py" in block` plus an echo guard that
' |', so the echo guard CANNOT FAIL, and the command assertion is a bare substring
satisfied by the echo's own argument. The adversarial lane replaced two graded step bodies
with `echo NO-OP scripts/<name>.py` and obtained 1988 passed / 83 skipped — the frozen
candidate's exact claimed result — with all guards at 0.
Separately, `policy_tests` — the ONLY step that runs pytest — appeared in ZERO tests, so
every 'the suite catches it' mitigation terminated at an unguarded step.
_authority: This contract is AUTHORED and thereafter FROZEN. Its independence property is precise and
worth stating honestly rather than overclaiming: the initial enumeration was seeded by
inspecting the workflow, exactly as tests/fixtures/expected-writable-roles.json was
originally seeded by reading the composition. What makes it an oracle is that it is NEVER
RE-DERIVED AT CHECK TIME. scripts/ci_invocation_model.py reads this file and the workflow
and requires the workflow to satisfy it; it never regenerates this file from the workflow.
So removing or neutering an invocation moves the OBSERVED side only, and is detected.
Changing this file is a reviewable diff and must be treated as one.
It does NOT claim to be derived from an independent specification of CI intent.
_contract: must_invoke lists targets that must be classified INVOKED by the shell analyser.
ECHOED, COMMENTED, ASSIGNED_NEVER_RUN, DEAD_BRANCH, AFTER_UNCONDITIONAL_EXIT, MASKED,
DEFINED_NEVER_CALLED, HEREDOC_DATA and UNKNOWN all fail. UNKNOWN fails closed on purpose.
Every graded id present in the workflow must appear here: a NEW graded step with no
invocation assertion is finding I24C-07's shape and is refused.
GATE 4N-I28Y. must_invoke alone is not a contract over a TEST command: Gate 4N-I28X added
`--deselect <node id>` to the graded pytest step, satisfied must_invoke perfectly, and
removed the whole assertion-control system from the run. required_options states what the
command MUST carry (the session-guard plugin); forbidden_options states the selection-
altering options it may never carry. Equivalent ordering and joined forms are handled.
This is a necessary condition only — the final authority on what ran is the session guard.

policy_tests.why_options_are_contracted: Gate 4N-I28X: `--deselect` on this step removed every mandatory assurance control while the step still invoked pytest and the contract still passed.
policy_tests.why_bootstrap_is_required: Gate 4N-I28AE closing ACC-I28AC-01: the bootstrap must establish executed-code provenance for the protected modules, and it must load BEFORE the session guard it protects.
policy_tests.why_home_isolation_is_required: Gate 4N-I28BH-E5: the strict bootstrap adjudicates the ambient Docker configuration surface (docker_boundary). A GitHub-hosted runner ships ~/.docker/config.json carrying registry 'auths', which the boundary declares FATAL_IF_PRESENT. This step consumes no Docker, so its strict-bootstrap pytest MUST run under a fresh, step-scoped HOME (a `$(mktemp -d)` directory set inline on the pytest command, established earlier in the same step) so no ambient ~/.docker can reach the boundary. DOCKER_CONFIG is not usable — the boundary declares it FATAL steering. HOME may not be a job/step-level env: key, because that would relocate the surface of the later image build/verify steps too.
